rules.statement: A statutory presumption in favour of the execution of a judicial or official act can be made if it is likely to have happened, considering the common course of natural events, human conduct, and public and private business.
rules.supporting_quote: This Court rules on a statutory presumption in favour of the execution, in terms of Section 114 (d) of the Evidence Ordinance. This Section reads as follows; 4 “The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct, and public and private business in their relation to the facts of the particular case – that judicial and official acts have been regularly performed.”
